name: Can I install a shower niche myself, or should I hire a professional?

mainEntity.name: Can I install a shower niche myself, or should I hire a professional?

acceptedAnswer.text:
You can install a shower niche yourself, but the difficult part is not cutting the opening; it is maintaining structural support, continuous waterproofing, correct slope, and a clean tile layout. A mistake may stay hidden until moisture damages the wall or the finish begins to fail.

Key factors:
- You need to identify studs, pipes, wires, and wall construction first.
- The niche must connect correctly to the shower waterproofing system.
- Tile layout and finished dimensions must be planned before cutting.

Practical guidance: DIY may be more realistic for an experienced remodeler who understands the chosen waterproofing system and tile work. If the shower is part of a larger bathroom renovation, consider having Elite Remodeling & Design coordinate the niche with plumbing, electrical, design, construction, and inspection requirements.

Do not treat a recessed opening as a minor cosmetic project inside a wet area.
acceptedAnswer.description: DIY is possible, but the niche must be framed, waterproofed, sloped, and tiled correctly while avoiding pipes and wiring. If you lack wet-area waterproofing and tile experience, professional coordination is safer, especially when the niche is part of a larger bathroom remodel.
